title: The phytochemical analysis of Carissa macrocarpa, cytotoxic potential of fractions, and the molecular modulation on p53 expression in HT-29 and LS174T cell lines.
authors: Alamri, Salma S; Alfaifi, Mohammad Y; Shati, Ali A; Elbehairi, Serag Eldin I; El-Kolobby, Dalia G; Hussein, Ahmed M; Mokhtar, Fatma Alzahraa
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物提取物对p53的调控及小分子-蛋白对接模拟，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，仅涉及小分子与p53蛋白结合，与本课题TF-DNA互作无关。
abstract: Natural products remain an invaluable source of anticancer agents, with flavonoids and phenolic compounds being particularly recognized for their ability to modulate tumour suppressor pathways. Carissa macrocarpa (C. macrocarpa) is an edible plant rich in secondary metabolites. This study sought to identify the secondary metabolites of C. macrocarpa leaves using LC-MS/MS, evaluate their cytotoxic and pro-apoptotic effects in colorectal cancer cell lines (HT-29 and LS174T), and elucidate potential molecular interactions with p53 through in silico docking, thereby uncovering mechanistic insights into its anticancer activity. LC-MS/MS revealed abundant flavonoid glycosides, particularly derivatives of kaempferol, quercetin, and isorhamnetin. Biological assays demonstrated potent cytotoxicity of the extracts, with the total extract showing the strongest effect against LS174T cells (IC(50) = 0.5 microg/mL). Extracts induced apoptosis, caused G1/S/G2 cell cycle arrest, and upregulated p53 expression. Docking confirmed strong binding affinities (-7.87 to -9.28 kcal/mol) for glycosylated flavonoids such as kaempferol-3-O-robinoside-7-O-rhamnoside, hesperidin, and isorhamnetin-3-O-rutinoside. Also, 100 ns molecular dynamics studies confirmed the stable binding of both kaempferol-3-O-robinoside-7-O-rhamnoside and hesperidin against the p53 pocket. In conclusion, this integrative study demonstrates that C. macrocarpa exerts anticancer effects in colorectal cancer cells by modulating p53 and provides a mechanistic rationale for its therapeutic potential.
abstract_zh: 天然产物仍然是抗癌药物的重要来源，其中黄酮类化合物和酚类化合物因其调节肿瘤抑制通路的能力而特别受到认可。Carissa macrocarpa（C. macrocarpa）是一种富含次级代谢产物的可食用植物。本研究旨在利用LC-MS/MS鉴定C. macrocarpa叶片的次级代谢产物，评估其在结直肠癌细胞系（HT-29和LS174T）中的细胞毒性和促凋亡作用，并通过计算机模拟对接阐明与p53的潜在分子相互作用，从而揭示其抗癌活性的机制见解。LC-MS/MS揭示了丰富的黄酮糖苷，特别是山柰酚、槲皮素和异鼠李素的衍生物。生物学实验表明，提取物具有强效细胞毒性，其中总提取物对LS174T细胞的作用最强（IC(50) = 0.5微克/毫升）。提取物诱导凋亡，引起G1/S/G2细胞周期阻滞，并上调p53表达。对接实验确认了糖基化黄酮类化合物如kaempferol-3-O-robinoside-7-O-rhamnoside、橙皮苷和isorhamnetin-3-O-rutinoside的强结合亲和力（-7.87至-9.28 kcal/mol）。此外，100 ns分子动力学研究证实了kaempferol-3-O-robinoside-7-O-rhamnoside和橙皮苷在p53口袋中的稳定结合。总之，这项综合研究表明，C. macrocarpa通过调节p53在结直肠癌细胞中发挥抗癌作用，并为其治疗潜力提供了机制依据。
